Give both directions of the exact orbit-invariance test and the single-constant test for \(f(p(x))/f(x)\), with a fixed sign convention for that constant. On two bits compute the table \(e^{i\theta(t\oplus c)}\), use the fixed control-zero columns to fix any common phase, and use a moved column to identify all angles. At \(\theta=\pi\) propagate a normalized two-term input through both orders, establish orthogonality, and explain equality of the basis-input output probabilities.

Construct two candidate devices with equal cycle products but inconsistent prescribed endpoints on a single cycle, and identify the specific failing arc.

C3s.D0_facet: D0 basis-action facet and its trace consequence. Tracks the label and phase after iteration of one edge, identifies return precisely at multiples of the cycle length, and derives the global power trace including the multiplicity factor \(|C|\). An equivalent cycle-block derivation of the same facts is accepted.
C3s.full_credit_work: Iterate the basis action and separate fixed labels of a power from nonreturning labels. Show that a length-\(\ell\) orbit contributes \(z^\ell-h_C\) to \(\det(zI-U)\) and contributes \(\ell h_C^{n/\ell}\) to \(t_n\) only when \(\ell\mid n\). For distinct lengths recover the product on the unique length-\(\ell\) cycle from \(t_\ell\) after subtracting all shorter divisor contributions, including the base case. With two fixed points and two transpositions, realize two assignments by unit phases and verify a common characteristic polynomial or equality of every trace, together with different within-length multisets. For the augmented observations, divide length-resolved traces by \(\ell\), use the first \(m_\ell\) power sums to reconstruct the monic polynomial of cycle products and all root multiplicities. Show that within-length permutations of products leave the reports invariant, and characterize unique labeled assignment for each length, including the cases of one cycle or identical products.

The example supplies realizable, genuinely different within-length multisets. The characteristic factorization verifies equality of the observational data for every power.
